ranking.rationale: Trip distance is the most domain-stable, causally relevant signal for taxi outcomes on WhyShift taxi, capturing core trip magnitude rather than calendar-specific or domain-identifying patterns. It should generalize better across temporal/domain shifts than month, week, hour, or minute features, and is less brittle than direction.

Hour of day adds strong, semantically stable signal for taxi outcomes beyond distance because traffic, congestion, and demand vary predictably by time-of-day across domains. It is generally more robust than week/month identifiers, less redundant than minute-of-the-day, and less likely than direction to encode location-specific or domain-specific artifacts.

Day-of-week adds stable demand and traffic-pattern signal beyond distance and hour, and is less likely than month or week to encode domain shifts tied to season or collection period. It is also more robust and semantically meaningful than minute-level timing or direction, which can be brittle across environments.

Direction adds route-structure information beyond distance and pickup time, and should remain semantically predictive across domains because fares/trip duration depend on origin-destination geometry and traffic corridors. It is less likely than month/week to encode domain shifts or seasonal identifiers, and minute_oftheday is largely redundant with hour.

Adds finer-grained within-day traffic variation beyond hour while remaining causally tied to travel time; it is more stably predictive than month or week, which are more likely to act as domain/time-period identifiers and capture seasonal or benchmark-specific shifts.

Month adds coarse seasonal signal that can stably affect taxi demand, traffic, and trip patterns beyond distance and time-of-week features, while being less domain-specific and less brittle than week-of-year, which more strongly encodes calendar position and potential split-specific artifacts.

Week-of-year may add limited residual seasonal signal beyond month, capturing recurring demand patterns like holidays and weather-related periods. Its marginal value is modest because month already covers most stable seasonality, but it is the only remaining candidate and is less problematic than location or demographic shortcut features.
